I. INTRODUCTION

children.text:
Transport phenomena in magnetic materials have been in-
tensively investigated, particularly Hall responses associated
with complex magnetic structures, such as the anomalous Hall
effect (AHE) and the topological Hall effect (THE). Initially,
the AHE manifests as a transverse voltage proportional to the
magnetization in ferromagnetic systems, even in the absence
of an external magnetic field [1–3]. Recent studies have re-
vealed that the AHE can be observed in noncollinear anti-
ferromagnets such as Mn3Sn [4], Mn3Ge [5]. To date, the
origin of the AHE has been extensively studied and is gener-
ally attributed to two main mechanisms: One is the extrinsic
mechanism, which arises from impurity scattering , including
skew scattering and side-jump [6–8]. The other is the intrin-
sic Karplus–Luttinger mechanism, originating from the Berry
curvature in momentum space [9, 10]. In contrast to the in-
trinsic AHE determined by the Berry curvature in momen-
tum space, the topological Hall effect (THE) originates from
the real-space Berry curvatures induced by chiral spin tex-
tures [11–13]. When conduction electrons propagate through
a noncoplanar spin configuration, they acquire a nozero Berry
phase that acts as an effective magnetic field in real space.
Such spin textures possesses a finite scalar spin chirality
(SSC), defined as χijk = Si · (Sj × Sk), where Si, Sj and
Sk represent spins at three neighboring atomic sites (i, j, k)
[1, 14, 15]. A nonzero SSC can arise in various noncoplanar
magnetic configurations, including skyrmion textures [16],
field-induced spin-reorientation states associated with a spin-
flop transition [17], and short-range spin clusters generated
by thermal fluctuations and magnetic fields [18–20]. Early
studies focused primarily on noncentrosymmetric B20-type
compounds, including MnSi [21], MnGe [16], and FeGe thin

where ρNxz, ρAxz and ρTxz represent the normal, anomalous, and
topological Hall resistivity, respectively. The normal resis-
tivity ρNxz is defined as ρNxz = µ0R0H, where R0 is the nor-
mal Hall coefficient. The ρxz exhibits a positive linear field
dependence at high fields, indicating that charge transport in
EuAuAs are dominated by hole-type carriers. The anomalous
Hall resistivity ρAxz = µ0RSM, where RS is the anomalous
Hall coefficient. The ρTxz denotes topological Hall resistiv-
ity, which derives from a real-space Berry phase acquired by
electrons upon moving through spatially varying spin textures
that possess finite SSC [11, 12, 14]. We use the Hall data mea-
sured at 2 K to illustrate the extraction of the normal, anoma-
lous, and topological contributions from the total Hall resis-
tivity [Fig. 3(b)]. A linear fitting of ρxz/µ0H versus M/µ0H
is performed in the field range 4 T ⩽ µ0H ⩽ 7 T, where
the magnetization is nearly saturated and the topological Hall
contribution is assumed to be negligible. The intercept and
slope are determined to be R0 = 0.735 µΩ·cm T-1 and RS =
0.208 µΩ · cm T-1, respectively. Using these parameters, we
calculate the the normal Hall resistivity ρNxz = µ0R0H and
the anomalous Hall resistivity ρAxz = µ0RSM. The topolog-
ical Hall resistivity is extracted as ρTxz = ρxz − ρNxz − ρAxz.

line corresponds to the topological Hall resistivity ρTxz, and the
dashed line is the baseline ρxz = 0. Inset of Fig. 3(b) shows
the field dependence of the extracted ρAxz over the temperature
range from 2 K to 8 K. The ρAxz is ∼ 0.19 µΩ cm at 2 K, and
gradually increases with increasing temperature.
